# embtrace-sbom 0.11.0 — four reader holes closed, one of them large

**If you produced a bill of materials with 0.8.4 – 0.10.0, run the tool
again.** Those versions could drop individual packages whose name is close
to another package's name, and a JavaScript project using a Yarn Berry
lockfile was read almost not at all. A new run restores them; nothing
needs to be uninstalled or cleaned up.

## Yarn Berry lockfiles are read

Yarn 2 and newer write `version: 4.4.0` with a colon; the reader knew only
Yarn Classic's `version "4.4.0"` and therefore returned **nothing** from a
Berry lockfile. What was left came from `package.json` manifests. Measured
on streamlit's frontend: 373 components before, 1,784 after (the embtrace
suite reads 1,778 from the same tree).

## A component's identity is its own name

De-duplication ran the name through the fuzzy matching form that strips
pkg-config component suffixes (`_core`, `_client`, `_base`, `_common`), so
that a CMake `GStreamer_video` matches a pkg-config `gstreamer`. Used as an
identity it merged packages that are not the same package, and the loser
left the bill silently. Measured across six real projects, nine packages
came back: `serde_core`, `playwright-core`, `puppeteer-core`, `tldts-core`,
`@sentry/node-core`, `@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base`,
`@docusaurus/utils-common`. Each has its own version and its own
vulnerability history.

## Your own tree is no longer counted as third-party code

* **Rust.** `globset = { version = "0.4.18", path = "../globset" }` is the
  normal layout of every multi-crate repository: the version is what gets
  published, the path is what this build uses. Your own crates were listed
  as third-party components. They now are not, unless the path names a
  different crate or cannot be resolved.
* **Python.** PEP 735 lets one dependency group include another
  (`all = [{ include-group = "dev" }]`). The group name was read as a
  package, so `dev`, `docs` and `linting` appeared as components.
* **Yarn.** `workspace:`, `link:` and `portal:` entries point into your own
  tree and are no longer components.

## A failed run now writes a local diagnosis file

If a reader crashes, the run continues with the other readers, says which
reader failed and that the bill is **incomplete**, writes
`embtrace-sbom-diagnosis.json` next to your SBOM, and ends with exit code
1. Nothing is sent: the file stays on your machine, and the run asks you to
mail it to support@innomatica.de if you want the defect fixed. It contains
the tool version, your Python version, the operating system, the reader,
the exception type and the call chain inside embtrace-sbom — no package
names, no versions, no paths, no file contents, no environment variables,
no host name. Open it and check; `tests/test_diagnosis.py` proves it with a
fabricated crash against canary data.

A build system that embtrace-sbom does not read yet is not a defect: the
run names it by label and count (`bazel (2), keil (1)`) and keeps exit
code 2.

## Windows

The test suite now runs on Windows as well as Linux, on Python 3.11 and
3.12.
